newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, more weakness expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, more weakness expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.29 percent on Wednesday and traders said the market would likely continue trading within a narrow range.
"Turnover will remain low and prices are most likely to continue falling, but it is hard to say when this trend will end," Toni Apollonio, an analyst at A bank said.
The SBI index fell 3.9 points to 1,334.36, the fourth consecutive day of losses. The index has lost 4.44 percent since March 13.
"The central bank's move decreased interest of foreign as well as domestic investors on such an unpredictable market and I cannot see any sign of this activity increasing," one trader said.

The Bank of Slovenia last month blocked foreign investment by demanding international investors to open special custodian accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in the country's securities.
Since February 11, when the bank made that move the index dropped 19.4 percent.
The banks are expected to open first custodian accounts at the end of March. They said the cost would be around 12 percent of the amount handled.
Overall six shares fell, five rose and two were unchanged, while 13 were untraded. Turnover rose, albeit marginally, to 83.2 million tolars from 64 million on Tuesday.
Drug company Lek's A issue was the most active share, easing 0.89 percent to 26,710 tolars on volume of 1,182 shares for total turnover of 31.4 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the biggest gainer, surging 10 percent to 6,600 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
Ordinary shares of trading company Kovinotehna led the day's decliners, falling 2.75 percent to 460 tolars on volume of 313 shares.
